title: bbox_describe_schema edge catalog is hand-maintained and narrower than what EdgeIndex projects
wanted_capability: bbox_describe_schema should derive its edge families and per-family kind lists from the same source EdgeIndex projects (or from an observed-kinds pass over the live edge sidecar), so the catalog agents orient on in step 1 of the opening sequence cannot drift behind the graph. Today the tool hand-lists families in crates/bbox-mcp-tools/src/mcp_tools/describe_schema.rs (~199-280): it advertises no Roadmap family at all although EdgeIndex reads roadmap stores and emits an eight-kind Roadmap family, and its Knowledge family lists only SUPERSEDES, DERIVED_FROM, Contradicts, KNOWLEDGE_FROM_SESSION, KNOWLEDGE_FROM_BOARD while KnowledgeEdgeKind::edge_kind() (crates/bbox-knowledge/src/knowledge.rs ~1073-1081) also emits RelatesTo, TensionWith, Supports, DependsOn, REFERENCES; thread structural edges (THREAD_SPAWNED_FROM/BLOCKED_BY/RELATES_TO/SUBSUMES) are likewise projected but not advertised. Found 2026-08-16 by the opus reviewer of the docs/retrieval-internals-refresh lane while re-grounding docs/graph-retrieval-internals.md against code; the doc now carries a one-sentence caveat about the mismatch, which is the workaround, not the fix.
missing_primitive: single-source edge-family catalog shared by EdgeIndex projection and describe_schema (or an observed-kinds enumeration)
fallback_used: docs/graph-retrieval-internals.md documents the full projected edge table and notes that describe_schema is narrower.
